name: Calf raise
pattern: Ankle plantarflexion: rise onto the balls of the feet and lower the heels, knees straight or bent.
setup: Balls of your feet on a step edge, heels free, feet hip width and pointing forward.
Knees straight but soft for standing raises; bent 90° for seated ones.
Hold a rail or wall lightly for balance.

steps.text: Let your heels sink below the step for a full calf stretch.
Push through the big toe and rise as high as you can.
Pause for a moment on your toes.
Lower slowly back to the stretch.

cues.cue: Full range: deep stretch to high on your toes.
cues.why: The calf raise is often cut short; a full range with a pause at the stretch makes each rep count.

cues.cue: Push through the big toe, ankle straight, not rolling out.
cues.why: Rolling onto the little toes shifts load to the outside of the ankle.

cues.cue: Knee straight for the gastrocnemius, bent for the soleus.
cues.why: Bending the knee lowers gastrocnemius activity, so the soleus does more.
Toes in slightly favoured the outer calf, toes out the inner calf; forward is balanced.
The Achilles tendon stores and returns energy; bouncing lets it do the work.

breathing: Breathe out as you rise, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Rise in 1 second, hold 1 at the top, lower in 2, brief pause at the stretch.

mistakes.name: Short range
mistakes.looks: The heel barely rises and never drops below the step.
mistakes.fix: Use less weight and take every rep from deep stretch to high toes.
mistakes.why: Half the movement, half the training effect.

mistakes.name: Bouncing
mistakes.looks: Quick rebounds at the bottom with no pause.
mistakes.fix: Pause 1 second in the stretch before rising.

mistakes.name: Knees bend to help
mistakes.looks: In a standing raise the knees dip and drive the body up.
mistakes.fix: Lock in a soft knee and keep it still.
mistakes.why: The quads and body bounce do the lifting instead of the calf.

safety: Achilles pain: slow lowering (heel drops) is a standard rehab method; build up under guidance.
Balance: hold a rail for standing and single-leg raises.
Do not drop deep into the stretch under heavy load until your calf is used to it.

variants.change: Knees bent about 90°: more soleus, less gastrocnemius.
One leg: twice the load per calf; hold support.
Hips bent about 90° with the trunk leaning forward: the hamstrings and gastrocnemius are stretched.

variants.when: leg press|calf press|hack|lever calf|bench press machine
variants.change: Push the platform with the balls of the feet; same ankle range, lying or seated.
From the floor: no stretch below level, shorter range.
Walk on your toes, heels high; loop as steps.
Raise the heels while holding a squat: soleus focus.
Heels drop below the step: full stretch.
Weight rolls around the foot; small range, balance focus.

easier: two-leg calf raise on the floor
harder: single-leg calf raise off a step

subtypes.name: Seated calf raise
subtypes.change: Seated, knees bent 90°, weight on the knees; ankle range the same.

subtypes.name: Tibialis raise
subtypes.change: Back against a wall, heels on the floor in front of you, lift your toes toward your shins: trains the front of the shin. Muscles: shins.

subtypes.name: Donkey calf raise
subtypes.change: Hips bent, trunk leaning forward on a support, legs straight.

metrics.label: Ankle angle
metrics.good: 10-20 at the bottom, -35 to -45 at the top

motion.basis: Ankle range estimated from typical active plantarflexion (about 40°) and step-edge dorsiflexion; knee angle effects from heberlosier2012; foot-angle effects from riemann2011.
